datasets.annotation_method: crowdsourced English data, professionally translated to 14 other languages

data_creator_info.evidence: We use the crowd-sourced English data that was professionally translated to 14 other languages for evaluation and the MultiNLI train set for training.

datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. Test sets are translations of English data.

datasets.translation_method: translation and re-annotation by XCOPA authors
datasets.annotation_method: translated and re-annotated from English COPA

data_creator_info.evidence: The XCOPA authors translated and re-annotated the validation and test sets of the English COPA dataset into 11 languages

datasets.notes: New to XTREME-R (not in XTREME). Training uses English COPA + Social IQa data. Test sets are translations.

datasets.variant_notes: XTREME-R always provides the full text of an input sentence, unlike XTREME which provided only lists of tokens.

data_creator_info.evidence: We employ the part-of-speech tagging data from the Universal Dependencies v2.7 treebanks covering 104 languages.

datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. 37 languages in XTREME-R selection (104 total in UD). Test sets are independently annotated.

datasets.variant_notes: XTREME-R adopts a more realistic version with no gold tokenization provided, meaning systems must use model-predicted tokens or tokenization-free approaches.
datasets.annotation_method: automatic annotation of proper noun spans in Wikipedia text as location, person, or organization

data_creator_info.evidence: For named entity recognition, we use the WikiANN dataset, in which proper noun spans in Wikipedia text have been automatically annotated as either location, person, or organization.

datasets.source_reference: Pan et al., 2017; Rahimi et al., 2019
datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. 47 languages in XTREME-R selection (176 total). Test sets are independently annotated. Uses balanced splits from Rahimi et al. (2019).

datasets.annotation_method: professionally translated from English SQuAD v1.1 subset

data_creator_info.evidence: A subset of the English SQuAD v1.1 dev set was professionally translated into ten other languages for XQuAD.

datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. Test sets are translations. Training on SQuAD v1.1.

datasets.translation_method: automatically mined from Wikipedia with crowd-sourced annotations and aligned answer spans
datasets.annotation_method: automatically mined from Wikipedia, annotations crowd-sourced, answer spans aligned

data_creator_info.evidence: The evaluation data in seven languages was automatically mined from Wikipedia, annotations were crowd-sourced, and answer spans aligned.

datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. Test sets are translations. Training on SQuAD v1.1.

datasets.variant_notes: Uses only the gold passage as context and excludes unanswerable questions — a simplification of the primary TyDiQA task.

data_creator_info.evidence: TyDiQA is a benchmark for information-seeking question answering, which covers nine typologically diverse languages.

datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. Test sets are independently annotated.

data_creator_info.evidence: We evaluate on the Tatoeba dataset, which consists of up to 1,000 English-aligned sentence pairs covering 122 languages.

datasets.notes: Retained from XTREME. 38 languages in XTREME-R selection (122 total). Fine-tuned on SQuAD v1.1. Test sets are translations.

datasets.variant_notes: Constructed specifically for XTREME-R. A more carefully sampled variant of Mewsli-9 linking against WikiData. Drops Serbian and adds Polish, Romanian and Ukrainian to obtain 11 languages.
datasets.annotation_method: automatically extracted from WikiNews hyperlinks to Wikipedia entity pages mapped to WikiData

data_creator_info.evidence: Mewsli (Multilingual Entities in News, linked) is an automatically extracted dataset that requires linking a contextual entity mention to its entry in a language-agnostic knowledge base.

datasets.notes: New dataset created for XTREME-R. Candidate pool ranges over 1M candidates across all 50 languages. Fine-tuning on English-only Wikipedia hyperlinks. Entity descriptions cover all 50 XTREME-R languages.

datasets.annotation_method: derived from XQuAD translations; each query has target answers in 11 languages

data_creator_info.evidence: We use the LAReQA XQuAD-R dataset which contains 13,090 questions each of which has 11 target answers (in 11 distinct languages) within the pool of 13,014 candidate answer sentences.

datasets.notes: New to XTREME-R. Fine-tuned on SQuAD v1.1 train set. Test sets are translations (derived from XQuAD). Models rank 13K candidates for each question.
